## What the chronicles say [Record]

Fought on 12 August 1399 on the Vorskla near present-day Poltava. [Vytautas](../characters/vytautas.qmd)'s coalition (Lithuanians, Ruthenian princes, Poles, Moldavians and Wallachians, some Order knights under [Marquard von Salzbach](../characters/marquard.qmd), and the exiled khan [Tokhtamysh](../characters/tokhtamysh.qmd)) was defeated by the army of [Edigu](../characters/edigu.qmd) and Khan Temür Qutlugh. About 50 princes fought under Vytautas and about 20 were killed, an estimate from Zenonas Ivinskis (1978); later accounts give far higher figures. The dead included Andrei of Polotsk and Dmitry (Demetrius) Starshy, Algirdas's sons, and Spytko II of Melsztyn. Temür Qutlugh proposed a three-day truce that was a trick to gain time and feigned a retreat to draw the Lithuanians from their wagon-fort; Tokhtamysh fled when he judged it lost. Vytautas barely escaped. Marquard, komtur of Ragnit, brought an Order contingent (en.wikipedia's 1,600 horse is unconfirmed); Posilge lists nine members of the Order killed and names Marquard among the rescued, and a Marienburg treasurer's entry of 2 Nov 1399 records the return of the money given for the unit. Consequences: Lithuanian expansion into southern Ruthenia was blocked, Smolensk, Novgorod and Pskov rebelled (Smolensk was recaptured in 1404), he reaffirmed the union with Jogaila and turned east to Moscow and west to the Order; he may have learned the feigned-retreat tactic he used at Grunwald. Sources: Długosz, Posilge, the Itinerarium Witolda, Ivinskis (Wikipedia, Battle of the Vorskla River). Treat the casualty numbers with caution.

## What really happened [Saga]

[Henė](../characters/hanulas.qmd) appeared to Vytautas as a messenger of the East with a vision of a golden throne and a crown at Sarai, and he accepted it in the winter, at which the pebble went cold. The Steppe-Hunger fed: dust devils walked beside the columns and horse-hair turned up in wells. The Root-Mother could not follow, so the wolves did not come; Kalvis and a few loyal wolves went anyway and died on the field. Perkūnas's verdict on a man who broke his oaths: Form 5 breaks. Vytautas escapes with a handful and no fog from his mother, shame only; he speaks the Five-Voice alone and pays the whole bill: sight and hearing dim, a face goes from memory. The Steppe-Hunger feeds on the field behind him.

## Consequences

Caused by [the Treaty of Salynas](ev_salynas.qmd) (which freed his western flank) and leading to [the Union of Vilnius and Radom](ev_vilnius_radom.qmd). Jadwiga's death on 17 July, a month earlier, is the last warning he ignored ([her death](ev_jadvyga_dies.qmd)).

## Dramatisation

Book II ch. 22 "Geležinis Maršas" (Spytko II), ch. 23 "Raudonas Dangus" (Vytautas), ch. 24 "Edigėjus" (Edigu; 11 August), ch. 25 "Dulkės ir Kraujas" (Spytko), ch. 26 "Skerdynės prie Upės" (Vytautas; 12 August), ch. 27 "Antrasis Bėgimas" (Vytautas) and ch. 28 "Kijevo Išpirka" (a Kyivan monk). High summer; the Book II climax.
